hypothesis: Compiling the stable repeated 20-block SANA-Video DiT path with PyTorch Inductor default mode will fuse lossless block glue and reduce the dominant denoising wall time; the first run also measures unavoidable cold compilation separately from the warmed request.

provenance.implementation: Enable only SANA_ENABLE_COMPILE=1; all other kernel/cache switches remain off. No runtime source or frozen workload change.

notes: The optional DeepGEMM import emitted a traceback and was disabled; BUILD_OK and the full run still completed with return code 0.
collect_run classified that non-fatal traceback as an error-pattern failure; the wrapper benchmark and output validity are authoritative for this round.

assessment.tool_limitation: The archived evaluator did not resolve BASELINE-LOCK.json and incorrectly requested lossy quality evidence; overlay kernel gating was applied instead.

validity.method_semantics: torch.compile changes graph lowering, fusion, scheduling, and floating-point operation order only. It retains the same SANA-Video mathematical modules, 50 scheduler steps, both CFG branches per step, all 20 transformer blocks per DiT call, BF16 transformer/text encoder, FP32 VAE, and no cache, sparsity, quantization, or model-work skip.
validity.visual_note: Authenticity-only inspection passed: first/middle/last frames show a coherent side-profile young man in the same sunlit forest, with plausible temporal pose/light evolution and no blank, corrupted, duplicated-baseline, or mismatched-content signal. No output-quality comparison was performed.

decision.reason: The cold compiled run is valid and its warmed request is 1.314x faster, but 117.41 seconds of first-use compilation makes the contract total 154.7 seconds, worse than the frozen 61.7-second baseline. Preserve the populated persistent compile cache and repeat the identical lossless config once as a hot-cache confirmation before retaining or rejecting compile.
